title: Binary gluing of a finitely presented module and a compatible map
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], W and V open subsets, and H a module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] such that H restricted to W is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let E be a finitely presented module on V, with a map j from E to H restricted to V whose restriction to W intersect V is an isomorphism. There is a finitely presented module G on W union V and a map phi from G to H restricted to W union V whose restriction to W is an isomorphism. No compactness, affineness, quasi-separatedness, or quasi-coherence is assumed, and no module outside W union V is constructed.

proof.text: On W intersect V the map j is an isomorphism. Use it as the identification between E on V and H restricted to W. The two-open cocycle follows from the inverse identities. Apply module-object descent on W union V to glue these modules.

The identity map to H on W and j on V agree on the overlap by the chosen identification. Morphism descent glues them to a map phi from the glued module G to H restricted to W union V. Its restriction to W is the gluing identification and hence is an isomorphism.

Finite presentation is local and invariant under isomorphism: transport the finite local presentations of H restricted to W and of E along the gluing identifications, and combine their covering families. This yields a finite local presentation of G. Neither compactness nor quasi-coherence is needed in this step.
